_note: Canonical export of design tokens. Mirror of tailwind.config.js + mobsf/static/mobinspect/css/src/app.css. No scripts/export-tokens.js exists yet — this file is manually maintained; keep it in sync by hand when either source file changes.

brand._note: The 'operate the tool' ramp: sidebar, topbar, logo, nav active-state, the global focus-visible ring (*:focus-visible on every interactive element), .btn-primary, .input focus border/ring. This is a deliberate, separate identity decision predating/independent of the CyberGuard-reference rebrand below — not an unfinished sweep.

500.use: base brand color — sidebar/topbar/logo, .btn-primary fill, .input focus border/ring, global focus-visible ring

brand._correction: The sidebar active-state (.mi-nav-item.is-active) was previously documented here as brand blue (#2563EB light / #60A5FA dark). Re-verified by pixel-sampling the actual CyberGuard reference (Dashboard.png) and found the real active-state chip is a neutral dark charcoal, not blue — see color.cta_black.use for the corrected token. This reverses an earlier, explicitly-confirmed decision to keep the sidebar on brand blue as a separate identity choice; the fidelity check to the source material took priority.

chart._note: Data-visualization duotone only — gauge fill, chart series, stat-tile accent bars/glows, non-semantic icon chips. Never buttons, nav, body text, or any other UI chrome (see the three-tier color/button policy note below). Hex codes sourced from the Behance 'Cyber Security UI/UX Design' (CyberGuard) reference's own style-guide slides — a client-material-pinned brief, not open-ended aesthetic guesswork.

amber.use: primary series — bars, line strokes, deltas, gauge fill

violet.use: secondary series — alternating bars, contrast line

chart.wcag_caveat: Both colors fail the 4.5:1 text-contrast threshold as a foreground text color (#FE4A23 on white = 3.38:1, #8D5CFC on white = 4.14:1, #8D5CFC on dark surfaces = 3.84:1), but both clear the 3:1 non-text/graphical-object threshold — fine for icon glyphs, chart marks, and large-display numerals; not fine for body text. A tree-wide audit for stray body-text usage ran the same session this token set was introduced.

severity._note: Semantic ONLY — signals a real scan-finding severity or connection/status health (VirusTotal detection ratio, tracker-count-vs-threshold, permission protection-level, audit-event risk category). Never used for decoration — see color.badge_neutral below for the correct default when a label carries no real severity meaning.

system._note: Interactive/status states — mirrors severity's passed/medium/critical/low hex values exactly (success=passed, warning=medium, error=critical, info=low).

score._note: Score tiers reuse severity's exact hex pairs — they are NOT a separate palette. Exposed as theme-aware CSS custom properties (--score-critical/medium/low/passed/unknown, defined in app.css's :root/[data-theme] blocks) rather than Tailwind static hexes, because inline style="color:" attributes (e.g. the gauge's SVG) can't resolve Tailwind's dark: class variants. ONE canonical threshold scale now lives in mobsf/MobSF/templatetags/mi_score.py (score_tier / score_color / score_class filters) — never hand-write the </30/<40/<60/else ternary in a template again. Before this filter existed, 7 templates each duplicated the threshold logic, and one (the analytics dashboard) used a different 3-tier scale entirely with no 'low'/blue tier, so the same numeric score could render a different color depending which page you were on.
score.thresholds: score < 30 -> critical | 30 <= score < 40 -> medium | 40 <= score < 60 -> low | score >= 60 -> passed

unknown.use: gauge_arc.html's fallback color when no score/color is supplied — deliberately gray, not brand blue (a real bug fixed this session: it previously silently defaulted to brand blue, which read as a false severity signal)

filters.score_color: value -> 'rgb(var(--score-<tier>))' ready-to-use CSS color (or '' if unset)
filters.score_class: value -> 'text-severity-<tier> dark:text-severity-<tier>-dark' Tailwind classes (or '' if unset)

badge_neutral._note: The newest severity-adjacent token, added to fix a real, systemic bug: severity-badge classes (badge-critical/high/medium/low/passed/unknown) were being reused across 15+ templates for purely decorative/informational pills with zero severity meaning — item counts ('75 endpoints', '4 categories'), version tags, feature labels, file-type tags. A green badge-passed pill next to an unrelated feature label reads as a false 'this passed a security check' signal. badge-neutral is the correct default for any label/count/tag with no real severity or status meaning.

cta_black._note: The .mi-pillbtn hero-CTA fill (mobsf/templates/base/app.html, #mi-chrome style block) — a dark grain-pill button, distinct from both the brand ramp and the chart duotone. Convention: exactly ONE hero CTA per dashboard-style page, matching the CyberGuard reference's single-primary-CTA-per-screen pattern. Pixel-sampled directly from Dashboard.png (RGB ~24-28/22-26/23-28) to confirm — an earlier pass mis-read this button as a light/cream fill from a compressed thumbnail; it is genuinely near-black.

dark.use: .mi-pillbtn background in dark theme (default); also .mi-nav-item.is-active background in both themes (sidebar active-state chip, corrected from brand blue — see color.brand._correction)

light.use: .mi-pillbtn background in light theme, via :root[data-theme="light"] .mi-pillbtn override; also .mi-nav-item.is-active background override in light theme

surface._note: Defined as theme-toggled CSS custom properties (--surface-0..4 in app.css's :root/[data-theme] blocks), NOT fixed Tailwind hexes — consumed via Tailwind's rgb(var(--token)/<alpha-value>) mechanism so opacity modifiers (e.g. bg-surface-2/50) keep working. Toggled via [data-theme="dark"|"light"] on <html>.

border._note: Theme-toggled CSS custom properties, not fixed hexes. See color.surface note.

text._note: Theme-toggled CSS custom properties, not fixed hexes. See color.surface note.

colorPolicy._note: The three-tier color/button policy — documented explicitly because the split otherwise looks like an unfinished/inconsistent sweep to anyone unfamiliar with the reasoning.
colorPolicy.1_operateTheTool: Brand blue (color.brand) = chrome for operating the tool: sidebar/topbar/logo/global focus-ring/.btn-primary/.input. A pre-existing, separate identity decision, not part of the CyberGuard visual mirror. EXCEPTION: nav active-state (.mi-nav-item.is-active) is NOT brand blue — pixel-sampling the reference showed a neutral dark chip, so it reuses color.cta_black instead (see color.brand._correction). This is the one piece of chrome fidelity-checking pulled back into the CyberGuard mirror.
colorPolicy.2_dataViz: Amber/violet (color.chart) = dashboard data-visualization content only: gauge, charts, stat-tile accents, non-semantic icon chips. Never chrome, buttons, or body text.
colorPolicy.3_heroCta: Dark grain-pill (.mi-pillbtn / color.cta_black) = the ONE hero CTA per dashboard-style page.
colorPolicy.4_severity: Severity system (color.severity / color.score) = semantic only, a real finding/status signal, never decoration — color.badge_neutral is the safe non-severity default.

family.display: 'Albert Sans', Inter, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif
family._note: Display (text-display, text-h1–h4): self-hosted Albert Sans (AlbertSans-Variable.woff2, SIL OFL license), applied via an explicit CSS override in app.css's @layer utilities rather than through tailwind.config.js's fontFamily — Tailwind v3's fontSize array-shorthand config has no fontFamily key (verified empirically, silently dropped from compiled output). Hex/typeface pairing for the display face came from the same CyberGuard reference style-guide as the chart duotone. Body/UI text stays on Inter (unchanged, self-hosted variable font), chosen deliberately over Albert Sans for small-size legibility in a data-dense tool — Albert Sans is a display-personality face used with restraint, not a UI-legibility one. Mono/data (JetBrains Mono, unchanged) covers hashes, code, technical values, tabular figures.

sidebar._note: Icon-only by default, with real localStorage persistence (key: 'mi-sidebar') — this app is a full-page-reload Django app (not an SPA), so without persistence an expanded sidebar would silently re-collapse on every navigation.
